question: Should experimental `claws update` be accepted into the stack with fail-closed `update_partial` recovery for package and Gateway mutations, once live recovery proof is supplied?
rationale: This is a new mutating lifecycle contract spanning independently owned external systems; tests can establish local behavior, but they cannot choose the acceptable operator-recovery guarantee or product scope.

options.title: Require proof and accept the scoped contract
options.body: Keep the executor fail-closed behind the experimental gate, require current-head package and Gateway recovery proof, then land only after the stacked planner base is ready.

options.title: Require stronger reconciliation first
options.body: Pause this slice until it adds an operation-identity reconciliation or another maintainer-approved recovery path beyond status/Doctor inspection and a fresh plan.

options.title: Defer the executor
options.body: Keep read-only planning and diagnostics while deferring mutation until the RFC and lifecycle ownership model have a confirmed landing sequence.

recommendation.title: Require proof and accept the scoped contract
recommendation.body: Keep the executor fail-closed behind the experimental gate, require current-head package and Gateway recovery proof, then land only after the stacked planner base is ready.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned and authored the current-head fixes for the executor’s latest partial-state and cron-ordering behavior.
